reason: the Go suite (unit, parity, placement, typography, full-corpus integration) - the core of the local gate every build-local / /build runs
the extension edition's node --test suite; Node is on the dev machine - until 2026-09-24 it sat in no runner at all, and the publish workflows build the extension without it
golangci-lint over the Go source; cheap, deterministic, same inputs as the test run
typos over the whole tree, including docs and site pages that no other check reads
structural Go<->JS drift on the change set; advisory (exit 3) inside the gate because a one-sided change is often intentional and is acknowledged by editing docs/PARITY.md

judges a produced artifact, so it runs where the artifact is produced - right after each local build, before the copy to the deploy folder; for a release it is a free local step in scripts/release.ps1 against the downloaded assets, because the tag workflow is paid and stays as it is
its input is a converted book the caller names; there is no fixed input a per-change runner could pass it, and it drives a headless browser for seconds per page
the corpus media is third-party work kept in the gitignored test_doc/ocrlab; on a clone without it the check can only say COULD NOT VERIFY, so it belongs to the OCR work that has the corpus
judges a scored run directory produced by ocrlab run + score, which takes minutes and a browser; it is the acceptance step of an OCR change, not of every change

the canon's own compliance check ships with the sza plugin, outside this repository; it is run when the canon is adopted or re-synced, and the plugin's hooks enforce the always-on part at the tool call
